description: The company's buildings (city building P0-C1, ARCHITECTURE decision 94) in a world 131072 x 98304 units (32 x 24 cells of 64 m), a managed company with $300,000 (30,000,000 cents) and no stations, so every cell is worth its empty base, 1,000 cents a m2. A managed company pays for a building: its floor at $40 (4,000 cents) a m2 and the right to use the land, the land value under its centre by its footprint. A house (512 m2 of floor, 256 of footprint) at (5000, 5000) costs 512 x 4,000 = 2,048,000 for the building and 256 x 1,000 = 256,000 for the land, 2,304,000 together: building 1, the balance 27,696,000. An office block (6,144 m2 of floor, 1,024 of footprint) at (40000, 40000) costs 24,576,000 + 1,024,000 = 25,600,000: building 2, the balance 2,096,000. A shop (1,152 and 576 m2) at (80000, 40000) would cost 4,608,000 + 576,000 = 5,184,000, more than there is: insufficientFunds, nothing changes. Demolishing the house costs a tenth of what it cost, rounded up: 230,400, the balance 1,865,600; building 1 is gone, and demolishing it again, or building 9, which never was, is unknownPlacedBuilding. Buildings are empty when built (no residents or jobs written). Every value worked out by hand.
